A point A on the ground is ${scope.d} m in front of a building TB. The angle of elevation of the top T of the building from A is ${scope.angle}°. Find the height of the building (rounded to 1 decimal place).
steps: Identify the known values in right-angled triangle $\triangle TAB$: adjacent side $AB = ${scope.d}\text{ m}$ and angle of elevation $\angle TAB = ${scope.angle}^\circ$.
Set up the trigonometric ratio using tangent: $\tan(\angle TAB) = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \dfrac{TB}{AB}$.
Substitute the values into the equation: $\tan(${scope.angle}^\circ) = \dfrac{TB}{${scope.d}}$.
Rearrange the equation by multiplying both sides by ${scope.d}$ to solve for $TB$: $TB = ${scope.d} \times \tan(${scope.angle}^\circ)$.
Calculate the result and round to 1 decimal place: $TB \approx ${scope.height}\text{ m}$.

${scope.svg}
A vertical cliff AC is ${scope.h} m above sea level. The angle of depression of a boat B from the top A of the cliff is ${scope.angle}°. How far is the boat from the cliff (rounded to 1 decimal place)?
steps: Use alternate interior angles to find the angle inside right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$: $\angle ABC = \text{angle of depression} = ${scope.angle}^\circ$.
Set up the tangent ratio in $\triangle ABC$: $\tan(\angle ABC) = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \dfrac{AC}{BC}$.
Substitute the known vertical height $AC = ${scope.h}\text{ m}$: $\tan(${scope.angle}^\circ) = \dfrac{${scope.h}}{BC}$.
Rearrange to solve for horizontal distance $BC$: $BC = \dfrac{${scope.h}}{\tan(${scope.angle}^\circ)}$.
Evaluate the expression and round to 1 decimal place: $BC \approx ${scope.dist}\text{ m}$.

The diagram shows a hot-air balloon B hovering above ground level AC with AB = ${scope.L} m. The angle of depression of A from B is ${scope.angle}°. Find the height of the balloon above the ground (rounded to 1 decimal place).
steps: By alternate interior angles, the angle of elevation $\angle BAC$ equals the angle of depression: $\angle BAC = ${scope.angle}^\circ$.
Identify the hypotenuse $AB = ${scope.L}\text{ m}$ and the vertical side opposite to $\angle BAC$, which is $BC$.
Set up the sine ratio in right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$: $\sin(\angle BAC) = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{BC}{AB}$.
Substitute the given values into the equation: $\sin(${scope.angle}^\circ) = \dfrac{BC}{${scope.L}}$.
Rearrange to solve for height $BC$: $BC = ${scope.L} \times \sin(${scope.angle}^\circ)$.
Evaluate the calculation and round to 1 decimal place: $BC \approx ${scope.height}\text{ m}$.

${scope.svg}
In the diagram, TF is a vertical building on level ground ABF, where AB = ${scope.AB} m. The angles of depression of A and B from T are ${scope.angleA}° and ${scope.angleB}° respectively. Find the height TF of the building (rounded to 1 decimal place).
steps:
Find the interior angles of non-right-angled triangle $\triangle ABT$:
• $\angle TAB = ${scope.angleA}^\circ$
• $\angle ABT = 180^\circ - ${scope.angleB}^\circ$
• $\angle ATB = ${scope.angleB}^\circ - ${scope.angleA}^\circ = ${scope.angleB - scope.angleA}^\circ$.
Apply the Sine Rule in $\triangle ABT$ to find length $AT$: $\dfrac{AT}{\sin(\angle ABT)} = \dfrac{AB}{\sin(\angle ATB)}$.
Substitute the angle values: $\dfrac{AT}{\sin(180^\circ - ${scope.angleB}^\circ)} = \dfrac{${scope.AB}}{\sin(${scope.angleB - scope.angleA}^\circ)}$.

Since $\sin(180^\circ - \theta) = \sin(\theta)$, rearrange to solve for $AT$: $AT = \dfrac{${scope.AB} \times \sin(${scope.angleB}^\circ)}{\sin(${scope.angleB - scope.angleA}^\circ)} \approx ${scope.AT}\text{ m}$.
In right-angled triangle $\triangle TFA$, set up the sine ratio for height $TF$: $\sin(\angle TAB) = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{TF}{AT}$.
Substitute $AT$ into the equation: $TF = AT \times \sin(${scope.angleA}^\circ) = ${scope.AT} \times \sin(${scope.angleA}^\circ) \approx ${scope.TF}\text{ m}$.

structures.questionTemplate:
${scope.svg}
Two points, A and B, are ${scope.AB} m apart on level ground and H is a helicopter above the ground between A and B. The angles of elevation of H from A and B are ${scope.angleA}° and ${scope.angleB}° respectively. Find the height of the helicopter above ground (rounded to 1 decimal place).
steps: Calculate the interior angle $\angle AHB$ in $\triangle ABH$: $\angle AHB = 180^\circ - ${scope.angleA}^\circ - ${scope.angleB}^\circ = ${scope.angleH}^\circ$.
Apply the Sine Rule in $\triangle ABH$ to calculate side $AH$: $\dfrac{AH}{\sin(\angle ABH)} = \dfrac{AB}{\sin(\angle AHB)}$.
Substitute known values: $\dfrac{AH}{\sin(${scope.angleB}^\circ)} = \dfrac{${scope.AB}}{\sin(${scope.angleH}^\circ)}$.
Rearrange to solve for $AH$: $AH = \dfrac{${scope.AB} \times \sin(${scope.angleB}^\circ)}{\sin(${scope.angleH}^\circ)} \approx ${scope.AH}\text{ m}$.
Consider the right-angled triangle formed by $H$, point $A$, and the point on the ground directly beneath $H$. Set up the sine ratio: $\sin(\angle HAB) = \dfrac{\text{Height}}{AH}$.
Rearrange to find the height: $\text{Height} = AH \times \sin(${scope.angleA}^\circ) = ${scope.AH} \times \sin(${scope.angleA}^\circ) \approx ${scope.height}\text{ m}$.

structures.questionTemplate:
${scope.svg}
In the diagram, AB is an advertisement board perched on a vertical pole BC. Points C and D are on level ground. AB = ${scope.AB} m, AD = ${scope.AD} m, and BD = ${scope.BD} m. Find the length of pole BC (rounded to 1 decimal place).
steps: Express $CD^2$ using the Pythagorean theorem in right-angled triangle $\triangle BCD$: $CD^2 = BD^2 - BC^2$.
Express $CD^2$ using the Pythagorean theorem in right-angled triangle $\triangle ACD$, noting that $AC = BC + AB$: $CD^2 = AD^2 - (BC + AB)^2$.
Equate both expressions for $CD^2$: $BD^2 - BC^2 = AD^2 - (BC + AB)^2$.
Expand the squared binomial $(BC + AB)^2$: $BD^2 - BC^2 = AD^2 - (BC^2 + 2 \times AB \times BC + AB^2)$.
Distribute the negative sign and eliminate $-BC^2$ from both sides: $BD^2 = AD^2 - 2 \times AB \times BC - AB^2$.
Rearrange the terms to isolate $2 \times AB \times BC$: $2 \times AB \times BC = AD^2 - BD^2 - AB^2$.
Solve for $BC$: $BC = \dfrac{AD^2 - BD^2 - AB^2}{2 \times AB}$.
Substitute the given values ($AB = ${scope.AB}\text{ m}, AD = ${scope.AD}\text{ m}, BD = ${scope.BD}\text{ m}$): $BC = \dfrac{${scope.AD}^2 - ${scope.BD}^2 - ${scope.AB}^2}{2 \times ${scope.AB}}$.
Calculate the value and round to 1 decimal place: $BC = ${scope.lengthBC}\text{ m}$.
